candidates.evidence: Consensus from 1 distinct detail proposals ([2821,2948]); weighted boundary [2821,2948], majority type trend. Representative evidence: Sustained, non-oscillatory monotonic rise after a shallow dip: from index 2821 (0.4) to 2914 (−0.7) then steep ascent to 3.1 at 2948. No peaks, troughs, or periodicity visible—entirely inconsistent with the robustly learned periodic motif (period ~183, 3 cycles per 549 pts). The final 34-point segment has slope ~+0.035, >15× steeper than the strongest drift in references (−0.0022). Boundary truncation cannot explain absence of any curvature across 128 points (>2/3 of period), and phase shift alone cannot eliminate all turning points. Full deviation from normal rhythmic behavior spans [2821, 2948].

Consensus from 2 distinct detail proposals ([2962,3018], [2972,3009]); weighted boundary [2962,3018], majority type shapelet. Representative evidence: A localized high-frequency spike train (6–7 sharp peaks within ~56 points) interrupts the otherwise smooth, monotonic descent after the second major peak. This motif deviates sharply from the learned normal pattern: normal decays are smooth with negligible curvature/roughness (roughness ~0.031), whereas this segment has abrupt sign changes and local amplitude >1.0 in robust z—unseen in any reference candidate. The burst is not phase-aligned with any known cycle and does not correspond to expected noise levels (MAD=0.698, so >2×MAD is extreme). | Counterevidence checked: Could be interpreted as transient sensor artifact or minor downsampling jitter—but the regularity and amplitude of the spikes exceed typical raster/downsampling artifacts, which are usually isolated or asymmetric; here the pattern is repetitive and structured over >50 points, inconsistent with benign truncation or phase shift. | Boundary rationale: Start at 2962: first clear upward inflection breaking the smooth descent (visible just after the main peak at ~2955); end

response.reason: Candidate 0 (proposed [2821,2948], trend) is not supported: the visible plot shows a normal quasi-sinusoidal cycle from ~2821 to ~2948 with a smooth peak near 2875 and symmetric descent—no monotonic rise or absence of turning points. The claimed steep ascent (slope ~+0.035) does not exist; instead, the curve descends smoothly after the peak, matching reference roughness (~0.031) and curvature (~0.014–0.016). The red band [2821,2948] overlaps a full, regular cycle, including a trough near 2914 and recovery toward the next peak—fully consistent with learned normal pattern. Thus candidate 0 is a false positive due to misinterpretation of phase/shape. Candidate 1 (proposed [2962,3018], shapelet) is verified: zoomed view shows a burst of 6–7 sharp, high-frequency oscillations (local amplitude >1.0 robust-z) embedded in the smooth descent after the peak at ~2955. This violates the learned normal motif’s smooth, low-roughness decay (roughness ~0.031 vs observed >0.1), and the pattern is repetitive over ~56 points—not explainable by downsampling, raster artifacts, or phase shift. Boundaries refined to [2962, 3018] (tight around the full burst), type confirmed as shapelet. Confidence remains high (0.94) due to clear morphological deviation and no benign alternative.

verified_anomalies.evidence: A localized burst of 6–7 sharp, high-frequency peaks (robust-z amplitude >1.0) interrupts the otherwise smooth, low-roughness descent phase. Normal decays have roughness ~0.031 and negligible curvature; this segment exhibits abrupt sign changes and structured oscillation over 56 points—unseen in any reference candidate and inconsistent with expected noise (MAD≈0.7, so >1.4×MAD). The morphology deviates fundamentally from the learned quasi-sinusoidal motif.
verified_anomalies.counterevidence: Checked against raster/downsampling artifacts: those are typically isolated, asymmetric, or single-point; this is repetitive, symmetric, and sustained over >50 points. Phase shift or truncation cannot produce such a dense, regular spike train within a smooth descent envelope.
